title: Normalized blowups preserve quasi-projectivity over an excellent affine base
statement:
Let $A$ be an excellent Noetherian ring [def-exc-excellent-ring], put $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $X$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] of finite type over $S$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose $X$ admits a locally closed immersion into $\mathbf P^m_S$ for some $m\geq0$. Let $J\subset\mathcal O_X$ be a nonzero finite-type quasi-coherent ideal [pqf-def-coherent]. Write $p:Z=\operatorname{Bl}_JX	o X$ for the ordinary blowup: on an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset X$, its charts are $\operatorname{Spec}R[J/a]$, for nonzero members $a$ of a finite generating set, where $R[J/a]\subset\operatorname{Frac}R$ is generated by $R$ and $j/a$ for $j\in J$. Let $
u:N=Z^
u	o Z$ be normalization in the function field [def-sc-normalization]. Then $Z$ and $N$ are integral Noetherian schemes, where Noetherian means quasi-compact and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Both are of finite type over $S$ and admit locally closed immersions into finite-dimensional projective spaces over $S$. The morphism $
u$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and $p\circ
u:N	o X$ is projective in the global finite-projective-space convention [def-kun-projective] and birational, meaning an isomorphism between dense open subschemes.
